name: TEXANS FOR A CONSERVATIVE MAJORITY
summary: Works to re-elect Senator John Cornyn of Texas — its money against candidates went to opposing his primary challenger Ken Paxton. Funded by large Republican donors and Cornyn-aligned groups, some of which don't disclose their own donors.

name: PROTECT PROGRESS
summary: Promotes cryptocurrency-friendly Democrats. Part of the crypto industry's Fairshake network, funded mainly by Coinbase, Ripple, and the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz.

name: UNITED DEMOCRACY PROJECT ('UDP')
summary: The super PAC of AIPAC (the American Israel Public Affairs Committee). It spends for or against candidates based on their positions on Israel.

name: AMERICANS FOR PROSPERITY ACTION (AFP ACTION)
summary: The main super PAC of the Koch political network, founded by billionaire Charles Koch. Promotes conservative and libertarian-leaning candidates and low-tax, low-regulation policies.

name: DEFEND AMERICAN JOBS
summary: Promotes cryptocurrency-friendly Republicans. Part of the crypto industry's Fairshake network, funded mainly by Coinbase, Ripple, and the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz.

name: A STRONGER MICHIGAN
summary: Boosted Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. Funded almost entirely by Center Forward, a Washington nonprofit that does not disclose its donors.

name: JOBS AND DEMOCRACY PAC
summary: Backs Democrats who favor regulating artificial intelligence. Run by Public First, a network founded by two former members of Congress and associated with a funding pledge from the AI company Anthropic.

name: THINK BIG
summary: Spends against Democrats who favor regulating artificial intelligence. Part of the 'Leading the Future' network funded by AI industry figures, including OpenAI's president. Watchdogs have filed a federal complaint alleging it concealed some spending.

name: VOTEVETS
summary: A progressive veterans' organization that supports Democratic-aligned veterans running for office.

name: FIGHT FOR KENTUCKY
summary: Backed Republican Nate Morris for Kentucky's open Senate seat. Its largest donor was Elon Musk, who gave $10 million.

name: NORTH STAR DAWN PAC
summary: Supported Angie Craig in Minnesota's Democratic Senate primary. Most of its money came through a nonprofit that does not disclose its donors, so who ultimately paid for it is not public.

name: ILLINOIS FUTURE PAC
summary: Backed Juliana Stratton for U.S. Senate in Illinois. Funded mainly by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker.

name: SLF PAC
summary: The Senate Leadership Fund — the super PAC aligned with Senate Republican leadership, working to elect Republicans to the Senate. Donors include some of the party's biggest contributors.

name: LOUISIANA FREEDOM FUND
summary: Works to re-elect Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana — nearly all of its spending went to opposing his primary challenger.

name: STAND FOR NEW YORK PAC
summary: Funded entirely by billionaire Michael Bloomberg to elect his former aide Micah Lasher to Congress in New York.

name: PINE TREE RESULTS PAC
summary: Works to re-elect Senator Susan Collins of Maine. Funded by billionaires including Ken Griffin and Stephen Schwarzman; its spending went to opposing her Democratic challenger.

name: FAIRSHAKE
summary: The cryptocurrency industry's main super PAC, funded chiefly by Coinbase, Ripple, and the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz. Spends for crypto-friendly candidates and against critics of the industry, in both parties.

name: ELECT CHICAGO WOMEN AKA ECW
summary: Spent millions in a Chicago-area congressional primary under a women's-group name. Filings released after the election showed most of its money came from AIPAC's super PAC, plus large Chicago donors.

name: 314 ACTION FUND
summary: Recruits and funds Democrats with science, medical, and engineering backgrounds for public office.

name: ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT INC
summary: A new super PAC formed in February 2026. Who funds it and what it stands for is not yet publicly known — its filings are the only public record so far.

name: AMERICAN MISSION
summary: Spends for Republicans who oppose regulating artificial intelligence. Part of the 'Leading the Future' network funded by AI industry investors. Watchdogs have filed a federal complaint alleging it concealed some spending.

name: WIN IT BACK PAC
summary: A vehicle of Club for Growth, the conservative anti-tax group — it spends in Republican primaries for the group's preferred candidates and against those it opposes.

name: BOLD AMERICA
summary: The outside-spending arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus's BOLD PAC, working to elect Hispanic Democrats.

name: LONE STAR LIBERTY PAC
summary: Backed Ken Paxton's challenge to Senator John Cornyn in the Texas Republican primary — nearly all of its spending went to opposing Cornyn.

name: CONSERVATIVES FOR AMERICAN EXCELLENCE INC.
summary: Funded by finance billionaires Ken Griffin and Warren Stephens. Intervenes in Republican primaries, generally against candidates aligned with the House Freedom Caucus.

name: GLCF, INC.
summary: The Great Lakes Conservatives Fund — works to elect Republican Mike Rogers to the Senate in Michigan. Funded almost entirely by Texas oil billionaire Tim Dunn.

name: DEFENDING OUR VALUES PAC
summary: Backs Republicans who favor regulating artificial intelligence. The Republican-side arm of the Public First network, which is associated with a funding pledge from the AI company Anthropic.

name: AMERICAN PRIORITIES (AP)
summary: A pro-Palestinian super PAC formed in 2026 to counter AIPAC's spending in Democratic primaries. Funded by disclosed, mostly Muslim American business donors.

name: MAGA KY
summary: Created by Donald Trump's political operation to defeat Representative Thomas Massie in Kentucky's Republican primary. Funded by major Republican donors, partly through pass-through groups.

name: KEEP AMERICA GREAT PAC, INC.
summary: Works to elect Representative Andy Barr to the Senate in Kentucky. Funded heavily by groups that don't disclose their donors, plus the crypto exchange Crypto.com.
